reading: Each isolated marker casts both diagonals to the grid border; along the rays, a cell in a region of background colour r takes the colour of the marker that sits in an r-region.
verb: cast diagonal rays coloured by region

slots.sources: the isolated marker cells (one per region colour)
slots.rays: both diagonals through each marker, to the border
slots.colour: region colour r -> colour of the marker lying in an r-region

why: every diagonal through a marker is painted to the border; ray colour switches whenever the ray enters a region of the other background colour

reading: The 3x3 input is placed in the top-left of a 6x6 empty canvas, then every coloured cell trails down-right diagonally in its own colour to the border.
verb: draw diagonal trails on doubled canvas
why: output is 2x the input size, top-left block equals the input, other blocks empty before extension; each fg cell's down-right diagonal is filled with its colour to the border
invariants: original cells keep position and colour

reading: Only the middle column is kept; every cell outside it is cleared to background.

new_rows.name: off_mid
new_rows.datalog:
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
midcol(X) :- px(Y, X, C), wmax(M), M = X + X.
off_mid(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !midcol(X).

why: every non-background cell outside the centre column becomes 0; the centre column is unchanged

reading: Each 0-shape is a 3x3 cap with a straight tail running to the far border; the cap slides along its tail to the far end and the tail is erased.
verb: slide cap to end of its tail

slots.subject: each 3x3 cap (0 ring with inner 7/9 cells) attached to a one-cell-wide 0 line
slots.path: the cap's tail line, ending at the opposite grid border
slots.result: cap copied unchanged at the tail's far end, touching the border; tail and old cap cleared to background

why: the cap pattern is identical before and after, now flush with the opposite border; no tail cells remain
invariants: stray 9 cells not part of a cap

reading: Rows (or columns) that have a 4 at both grid edges are recoloured between the 4s by swapping 0<->8 and 6<->7.

new_rows.name: bracketed
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowpair(Y) :- px(Y, 0, 4), wmax(W), px(Y, W, 4).
colpair(X) :- px(0, X, 4), hmax(H), px(H, X, 4).
bracketed(Y, X) :- rowpair(Y), px(Y, X, C).
bracketed(Y, X) :- colpair(X), px(Y, X, C).

why: on each line bounded by 4s at opposite edges, every cell a becomes key(a) with key = {0->8, 8->0, 6->7, 7->6, 4->4}; all other cells unchanged

reading: Around every isolated 1 a fixed plus is stamped: 2 above, 7 left, 6 right, 8 below (clipped at the border).
why: each marker is the centre of an identical 3x3 plus (2 up, 7 left, 1 centre, 6 right, 8 down); nothing else changes

reading: Inside the 2-frame, everything is filled with 2 except the bounding box of the 5 cells, which stays as it was.

new_rows.name: frame_minus_box
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
big(max(N)) :- osize(O, N).
frameobj(O) :- osize(O, N), big(N).
inner(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), obj(O, Y, X), !frameobj(O).
fy0(min(Y)) :- frameobj(O), obj(O, Y, X).
fy1(max(Y)) :- frameobj(O), obj(O, Y, X).
fx0(min(X)) :- frameobj(O), obj(O, Y, X).
fx1(max(X)) :- frameobj(O), obj(O, Y, X).
iy0(min(Y)) :- inner(Y, X).
iy1(max(Y)) :- inner(Y, X).
ix0(min(X)) :- inner(Y, X).
ix1(max(X)) :- inner(Y, X).
inbox(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), iy0(A), iy1(B), ix0(P), ix1(Q), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= P, X <= Q.
frame_minus_box(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), fy0(A), fy1(B), fx0(P), fx1(Q), Y > A, Y < B, X > P, X < Q, !inbox(Y, X).

why: every frame-interior cell outside the 5s' bounding box becomes 2; the box and everything outside the frame are unchanged
invariants: 5 cells and the 0 cells inside their bounding box

reading: The 5x5 input uses a single colour; the output is a fixed 3x3 glyph in 5 picked by that colour: 1 -> plus, 2 -> T (top row + middle column), 3 -> L (right column + bottom row).
why: pairs with the same input colour have identical outputs; the cell layout of the input does not matter

reading: Count the T-shapes with stem up and with stem down; output a fixed 3x6 grid whose left 3x3 shows the stem-up count as 3-dots and right 3x3 the stem-down count as 1-dots, at corner positions 1:(0,0); 2:(0,0),(2,0); 3:(0,0),(0,2),(2,0); 4: all four corners.
verb: count shape kinds as dot glyphs

slots.items: T-tetrominoes of colour 2 (222 over a centre stem)
slots.classes: stem pointing up vs stem pointing down
slots.output: fixed 3x6 canvas; left half corners get colour 3 for the stem-up count, right half corners get colour 1 for the stem-down count, using the count-glyph pattern

why: number of 3s equals the number of stem-up Ts and number of 1s equals the number of stem-down Ts, positions given by a fixed per-count pattern

reading: Each complete multi-coloured template appears once; elsewhere a few cells of it appear as fragments, and each fragment is completed into a full copy of the template whose same-coloured cells match it.

slots.templates: each multi-coloured 8-connected shape (there can be more than one per grid)
slots.fragments: small groups of loose cells whose colours and relative offsets match a sub-pattern of one template
slots.placement: copy of the matching template positioned so the fragment cells coincide with its same-coloured cells

why: every fragment ends up inside an exact copy of a template; templates and background unchanged
